learningObjectives: Explain how Java applications communicate over HTTP.
Construct basic HTTP requests using Java HTTP Client.
Handle responses, status codes, and request failures safely.

activities.title: HTTP Request Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the main parts of an HTTP request.

content.concept: An HTTP request can contain a method, target URL, headers, and an optional request body. These components tell the server what operation is being requested and provide any required data.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Defines the requested operation, such as GET or POST.
Identifies the server resource being requested.
Carries metadata such as content type or authorization information.
Carries data sent to the server when the request requires a payload.

activities.title: HTTP Request Flow
activities.instruction: Arrange the steps of a Java HTTP request in the correct order.

content.concept: Java's HTTP Client creates a request, sends it to the server, receives an HTTP response, and then the application processes the response.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

goal: 5. Process the status code and response body

activities.title: Build an HTTP Request
activities.instruction: Construct the essential parts of a Java HttpRequest.

content.concept: A Java HttpRequest can be configured with a target URI, HTTP method, headers, and an optional body before it is sent through HttpClient.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: HTTP Status Codes
activities.instruction: Identify what each HTTP status-code category communicates.

content.concept: HTTP status codes are grouped into categories: 2xx indicates success, 3xx indicates redirection, 4xx indicates a client-side request problem, and 5xx indicates a server-side failure.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: The request was successfully received and processed.
The client may need to follow another location or handle a redirection.
The request has a problem from the client's side, such as an invalid request or missing authorization.
The server encountered a problem while processing a valid request.
